title: Who or what?
en: Name the person or thing doing an action.
tip: 이 follows a final consonant; 가 follows a vowel. 누구 + 가 becomes 누가; 저 + 가 becomes 제가.

title: Describe something
en: Say what something is like.
tip: 좋다 uses 이/가 for what is good; 좋아하다 takes 을/를 for what you like.

title: Set a topic
en: Give information about a topic or make a contrast.

examples.en: I have a lot of time today.

tip: 은 follows a final consonant; 는 follows a vowel. A topic is not automatically the subject. 이/가 is not limited to new information.

title: Objects of actions
en: Name what you eat, read, watch, write or study.

examples.en: My younger sibling eats a meal.

tip: 을 follows a final consonant; 를 follows a vowel.

title: Have or do not have
en: Say what exists or what you have.

title: Names and identities
en: Say what something or someone is.
tip: 이에요 follows a final consonant; 예요 follows a vowel. These forms already appeared in the source.

title: Where something is
en: Locate a person or thing.

examples.en: The bag is in the classroom.

title: Destinations and arrival
en: Name a destination.

examples.en: The taxi arrives at the airport.
My friend comes to my home.

title: Where an action happens
en: Say where you study, eat, work or meet.

examples.en: My friend waits at the cafe.
The student learns Korean in the classroom.

title: Relative positions
en: Use a location noun before the place particle.

examples.en: The pharmacy is in front of the convenience store.
The phone is inside the bag.
We meet in front of the school.
The book is under the desk.

title: Home and distance
en: Talk about where you live and nearby places.

examples.en: My home is near the station.
My workplace is far from home.
There is a cafe near my home.

tip: 살다 can use 에 or 에서. 에서 also marks a reference/source point in the distance example; it is not always an action location.

title: Transportation
en: Say how you travel.

examples.en: I go to school by bicycle.
I go to Korea by plane.

tip: 으로 follows a final consonant except ㄹ. 로 follows a vowel or ㄹ: 버스로, 지하철로, 자동차로.

title: Directions and routes
en: Say which way to go.

examples.en: I go slowly to the left.

tip: 에 emphasizes the destination; (으)로 can emphasize direction. They overlap in some contexts but not everywhere. The original request form 가세요 is listed in the grammar extension.

title: Tools and payment
en: Say which tool or means you use.

examples.en: I write my name with a ballpoint pen.
I take photos with a camera.
I send a file using a computer.
I buy a gift with a card.

title: Materials
en: Say what you make something out of.

examples.en: I make a desk out of wood.
I make a gift out of paper.
I make a cup out of glass.
I make a cup out of plastic.

title: Languages
en: Name the language you use.

title: Roles and jobs
en: Say in what role someone works.

title: Also / too
en: Add another person or thing to the same statement.

examples.en: My younger sibling eats bread too.

tip: At this level, 도 replaces 이/가, 은/는 or 을/를. It may follow other particles: 집에서도, 친구한테도. This is not a universal ban on particle combinations.

title: Only
en: Limit the statement to a person or thing.
tip: Compare the scope: 저만 커피를 마셔요 = only I drink coffee; 저는 커피만 마셔요 = coffee is the only thing I drink in this context.

title: Possession
en: Connect an owner or relationship to a noun.

examples.en: I look at a family photo.

tip: 저의 often contracts to 제. 의 may be omitted in natural noun combinations: 한국어 단어 is more natural than 한국어의 단어 for Korean vocabulary.

title: Give to someone
en: Name the recipient of something.

examples.en: I give my friend a gift.

tip: 한테 is conversational; 에게 is neutral/written. People and animals normally take these; ordinary places take 에.

title: Send to someone
en: Name who receives a message or item.

examples.en: I send a letter to my friend.
I send a message to my colleague.
I send an email to the professor.
I send photos to my family.

title: Communicate with someone
en: Name who hears the information.

examples.en: I ask my neighbor for help.
I share news with a relative.

title: Tell and teach
en: Add both a recipient and the information.

examples.en: I tell the nurse the address.
I tell the junior colleague the phone number.
I teach Korean to a foreign learner.
I ask a police officer for directions.

title: Attitudes toward people
en: Say who you feel thankful toward or treat kindly.

examples.en: I am grateful to my senior colleague.

title: One connected story
en: Use several short sentences instead of one overloaded sentence.

examples.en: I go to the cafe by bus.
I meet a friend at the cafe.
I give my friend a gift.
